clue.text: Eat from river, as bird

indicators.note: from here means taken away from, so the word eat is removed out of the river's name

parts.note: the Great Ouse is a river in eastern England
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bird is described as feeding from a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eat' looks like the verb of the surface, but it is the letters EAT, removed by 'from' out of GREAT OUSE, leaving GR + OUSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The red grouse is a game bird of British moorland, shot for sport.

clue.text: Sign of hinge being forced — suggesting chip shop shut?

indicators.note: a forced hinge is wrenched out of shape, so the letters are wrenched into a new order

explanation.surface: A broken hinge on the door suggests the chip shop is closed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being forced' rearranges SIGN OF HINGE. A chip shop is a British fish-and-chips takeaway; this notice says the owner has left for the day.
explanation.definitionFit: A notice saying the owner is off with rod and line is a jokey sign that a shop is closed, apt for a fish shop.

clue.text: Oedipus complex, God's work

indicators.note: complex means intricate or tangled, so the letters are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Freud's Oedipus complex is held up as divine work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' looks like part of the psychological term, but it signals rearranging OEDIPUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus Dei is Latin for 'work of God', also the name of a Catholic organisation.

clue.text: Marine creature some observe as natural in the drink

indicators.note: in puts the hidden run inside the drink

parts.note: sake is the Japanese rice wine, a drink

indicators.note: some means only part of these words is taken, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Some people watch a marine creature as if it were natural in the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks EASN from observE AS Natural, which goes 'in' SAKE. 'the drink' suggests the sea, but it is sake.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea snakes are venomous reptiles living in warm tropical seas, a marine creature.

clue.text: Airmen heading for fog in torment, seeking fuel

indicators.note: in places the airmen and the fog's first letter inside the word for torment

parts.note: torment means pain
the RAF, Royal Air Force, is a body of airmen

indicators.note: the heading for a word is its first letter, here taken from fog

explanation.surface: Pilots flying into fog, in agony, are desperate for fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Airmen' is the usual crossword pointer to the Royal Air Force, not to individual pilots.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraffin is kerosene, burned as a fuel in heaters, lamps and jet engines.

clue.text: Changes impressing upon women where children should be entertained

indicators.note: impressing means pressing in, so the word for changes takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: alters means changes
onto means upon

explanation.surface: Changes that impress upon women where their children should be amused.
explanation.walkthrough: Alton Towers is a large British theme park in Staffordshire, so the definition needs that bit of UK knowledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Alton Towers is a theme park, a place where families take children for rides and fun.

clue.text: Might it prove hairy having to equip mine?

parts.note: to arm is to equip with weapons
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A miner wonders whether equipping the pit will be hairy, meaning risky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hairy' reads as risky or scary, but it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: The armpit is a part of the body where hair grows, so it may well be hairy.

clue.text: See 1
Excite reactions — or not?

indicators.note: to excite is to stir up, so the letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Stir up responses, or perhaps don't.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excite' rearranges REACTIONS; 'or not?' turns the whole clue round to define the opposite of exciting.
explanation.definitionFit: To narcotise is to dull with a drug, the reverse of exciting, so 'or not' points to it.

clue.text: Sweet name, posh one, almost rejected

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the whole run of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: a tag is a name or label
U is the crossword abbreviation for upper-class, posh

indicators.note: almost means the word one loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A snobbish person nearly turns down a named sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the whole run at once, after 'almost' has trimmed the final letter from one.
explanation.definitionFit: Nougat is a chewy confection of sugar or honey with nuts, a classic sweet.

clue.text: Fine sprays via this form are moist

indicators.note: to form something is to shape it, so these letters are shaped into a new word

explanation.surface: The letters of a moist mixture form a device for fine sprays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form' signals rearranging the eight letters of ARE MOIST.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomiser is a device that turns liquid such as perfume into a fine spray.

clue.text: So my resentment is not to be trusted? Thanks!

definitions.text: So my resentment is not to be trusted? Thanks!

parts.words: So my resentment is not to be trusted? Thanks!
parts.note: the stock polite phrase for accepting an offer, read as saying that if I do mind, that minding cannot be relied on

annotation.spelling: I DON'T MIND IF I DO

explanation.walkthrough: Read the phrase as 'I don't mind if I do (mind)': my resentment is unreliable. The everyday sense is a polite yes to an offer, so 'Thanks!' is the plain definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a cheerful way of accepting something offered, much like saying yes please.

clue.text: Football team given assignment as release from slavery

parts.note: Man U is short for Manchester United, the English football club
a mission is an assignment

explanation.surface: A football club is given a task to free slaves.
explanation.walkthrough: MAN U is everyday shorthand for Manchester United Football Club.
explanation.definitionFit: Manumission is the formal freeing of a slave by its owner.

clue.text: Steer past smart boy, seeking parking spots

parts.note: chic means stylish, smart
Ken is a boy's name
P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs
a steer is a young castrated bull, an ox

explanation.surface: A cow is driven past a well-dressed lad who is looking for somewhere to park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steer' looks like a verb steering past the boy, but it is the animal, placed last.
explanation.definitionFit: Chickenpox is a childhood illness known for its itchy red spots, so spots stands for the disease.

clue.text: Cleaner nation under fish wife

indicators.note: in a down clue under means placed below, so the nation comes after

parts.note: char is a fish related to the trout
Oman is a nation in Arabia

explanation.surface: A cleaner from a nation married to a fishmonger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' puts OMAN below CHAR + W in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A charwoman is a woman paid to clean houses or offices, a cleaner.

clue.text: Reportedly tasteless fruit

indicators.note: reportedly means as said or heard, so the word sounds like another

parts.note: something tasteless in style is ugly

explanation.walkthrough: 'Reportedly' says UGLY is spoken to give UGLI.
explanation.definitionFit: The ugli is a Jamaican citrus fruit, a cross of grapefruit and tangerine with knobbly skin.

clue.text: Lid keeps energy within metal pier structure

indicators.note: within places the lid with its energy inside the metal

parts.note: iron is a metal

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the lid holds the energy

parts.note: a cap is a lid
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A lid holds energy inside a metal pier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps' and 'within' nest one container inside another. An ice apron is a real engineering term, worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice apron is a wedge-shaped structure on a bridge pier that breaks up floating ice.

clue.text: Cultured group lacking leadership

indicators.note: lacking leadership means the word loses its leading, first letter

parts.note: a party is a group of people

explanation.surface: A cultured set of people without anyone in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking leadership' takes the P from PARTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Arty describes someone showily interested in the arts, a somewhat mocking way of saying cultured.

clue.text: See 24 across
Perfect, though inedible to hens, might one say?

indicators.note: a question about how one might say it means the word is heard, not spelt

parts.note: something hens cannot eat could be called un-peckable, here formed with the prefix im-

explanation.surface: Something flawless might be described as safe from a hen's beak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might one say' marks a sound-alike: a made-up word for not peckable sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Impeccable means faultless, without any flaw, which is perfect.

clue.text: Support troppus?

definitions.meaning: ... means support, as in giving a cause one's ...
the word support written back to front, a support read in reverse

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is a pun: TROPPUS is SUPPORT spelt backwards, so it is support going in reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Backing is support, and also describes a word going backwards, as troppus does.

clue.text: Bother about Religious Instruction? He should!

definitions.text: Bother about Religious Instruction? He should!

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for bother goes around the other piece

parts.note: a pest is a bother, a nuisance
RI is the abbreviation for Religious Instruction, a school subject in Britain

explanation.surface: Should someone worry about religious teaching? A clergyman certainly should.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: a cleric ought to care about religious teaching.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest is a member of the clergy, whose job is to teach and care about religion.

clue.text: Ability to withstand blast in car witnessed after explosion

indicators.note: an explosion blows things apart, so the letters are scattered and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Something seen in a car after a bomb tests how well it withstands the blast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after explosion' signals rearranging all fourteen letters of IN CAR WITNESSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Wind resistance is how well something holds up against moving air, a blast of wind.

clue.text: Dressed in yellow and white?

parts.note: covered in the yolk and white of a hen's breakfast staple, not clothed in those colours

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dressed' suggests clothes, but think of a food coated in yolk and white.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggy means covered in or tasting of egg, which has a yellow yolk and a white.

clue.text: Capture in wonderful drawing?

indicators.note: in places the word for capture inside the word for wonderful

parts.note: magic as an adjective means wonderful
to net something is to capture it

explanation.surface: A wonderful picture is captured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawing' looks like a picture, but it means pulling toward, as a magnet does.
explanation.definitionFit: Something magnetic attracts, drawing things toward it.

clue.text: In panic, Goons' song cut short — suggesting chip shop open?

indicators.note: In puts the shortened song inside the word for panic

parts.note: fright is panic

indicators.note: cut short means the song title loses its last letter

parts.note: The Ying Tong Song was a 1956 novelty hit by the Goons, the British radio comedy team

explanation.surface: Someone in a panic hears a clipped Goons song, a sign the chippy is open.
explanation.walkthrough: The Goon Show was a 1950s BBC radio comedy. A chip shop is a British fish-and-chips takeaway, where this notice means it is trading.
explanation.definitionFit: A notice saying the fryers are on tonight is the traditional sign that a fish-and-chip shop is open.

clue.text: Composing music, Beethoven's Fifth removed from love?

indicators.note: removed from means one letter is taken out of the longer phrase

parts.note: love can be described, teasingly, as the condition of not hating

indicators.note: the fifth letter of the word Beethoven's is picked out

explanation.surface: A composer's fifth symphony is taken away from someone dear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beethoven's Fifth' sounds like the symphony, but it is H, the fifth letter of Beethoven, removed from NOT HATING.
explanation.definitionFit: Notating is writing music down in notation, a part of composing it.

clue.text: Return of weapon in secret so fitting?

indicators.note: in places the turned weapon inside the word for secret

parts.note: sly means secretive, done on the quiet

indicators.note: return means come back, so the word for weapon is read backwards

parts.note: a gun is a weapon

explanation.surface: A weapon secretly comes back, which seems fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return of' turns GUN to NUG, which goes 'in' SLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Snugly means in a close-fitting way, so it describes how something fits.
